label: Institution
name: National University of Costa Rica
summary:
The National University of Costa Rica (Universidad Nacional, UNA, founded 1973 in Heredia) is one of Costa Rica's four public universities, established as part of the remarkable expansion of Costa Rican public higher education in the 1970s under President Daniel Oduber Quirós — a period when Costa Rica systematically invested in accessible public university education as part of its exceptional commitment to democratic development, social equity, and education-based human capital that has made Costa Rica one of Latin America's most stable democracies.

Costa Rica's commitment to education as a national priority is extraordinary in the Latin American context: the country abolished its military in 1948 (the abolition declared by President José Figueres Ferrer, inscribed in the 1949 Constitution), redirecting military spending to education and health. This decision — unique in world history for a state voluntarily abolishing its armed forces — created the conditions for sustained educational investment that made Costa Rica a regional educational leader. The 1973 founding of UNA (alongside ITCR and the later UNED) was part of this educational investment strategy.

The National University of Costa Rica focuses particularly on environmental sciences, humanities, social sciences, and education — areas that reflect Costa Rica's national priorities. The university's environmental programs align with Costa Rica's extraordinary commitment to ecological conservation: the country has protected approximately 26% of its territory as national parks and reserves, making it a world leader in biodiversity conservation. UNA's research on tropical biodiversity has contributed significantly to global environmental science.
